module_title: Coastal Plains - Regional Divisions and Water Channels
introduction: At this level, we dive into the regional/local names of the coastal plains, the concept of Kayals (backwaters), and the specific maritime channels (8° and 9°) that separate the islands.

core_concepts.title: West Coast Divisions (North to South)
core_concepts.description: 1. Kathiawar/Kachchh Coast (Gujarat), 2. Konkan Coast (Maharashtra to Goa), 3. Kannad Coast (Karnataka), 4. Malabar Coast (Kerala).

core_concepts.title: East Coast Divisions (North to South)
core_concepts.description: 1. Utkal Coast (Odisha), 2. Northern Circars (Southern Odisha to Andhra Pradesh), 3. Coromandel Coast (Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu).

core_concepts.title: Kayals (Backwaters)
core_concepts.description: On the Malabar coast of Kerala, sea water flows into the land creating shallow lagoon lakes, locally called 'Kayals'. 'Vembanad' is the longest lake in India and a famous Kayal where the Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held.

core_concepts.title: 8 Degree and 9 Degree Channels
core_concepts.description: The 8° Channel separates 'Maldives' (the country) from 'Minicoy' (the southernmost island of Lakshadweep). The 9° Channel separates 'Minicoy' from the 'Rest of Lakshadweep'.

important_entities.name: Barren Island
important_entities.significance: Located in the Andaman Sea. Nearby is 'Narcondam' Island, which is a dormant volcano.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Malabar Coast (Kerala) gets the 'first' rain from the South-West Monsoon in summer. However, the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu) remains mostly dry in summer and receives its bulk rainfall in 'winter' from the retreating (North-East) monsoon.

exam_strategy_tips: Match the coastal names (Konkan, Malabar, Coromandel) to their respective states perfectly; this is highly tested.
Remember that the highest peak of Andaman and Nicobar is 'Saddle Peak' (732m), located in North Andaman.
